fact_ledger: aswang is a general term for shape‑shifting evil creatures in Filipino folklore
Spanish colonists in the 16th century recorded aswang as the most feared Philippine myth
aswang categories include vampire, manananggal (viscera sucker), weredog, witch, and ghoul
manananggal sheds its lower half at night, grows wings, and uses a narrow tongue to suck organs
aswang fear light and noise, and can live near villages or in forests
aswang can infiltrate villages by marrying into the community
witch aswangs curse victims, causing rice, bones, or insects to emerge from bodies
protective remedies include holy objects, salt, vinegar, and the tail of a stingray
aswang are especially feared in southern Luzon, Mindanao, and Visayas, notably Capiz
the aswang attacks pregnant women and unborn children
